packed_tags.subject: science
packed_tags.topic: What is living; diversity, life cycles and plant processes

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Larvae and eggs repeatedly rise to the surface for air, and kerosene stops both from breathing.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Kerosene cuts off air to all larvae even when they can reach uncovered gaps at the surface.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Adult mosquitoes must return to the water surface to breathe, so the kerosene layer suffocates them too.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: A transparent kerosene layer will not stop larvae breathing because air can pass through it.

intelligence.enrichment: Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water but require air to respire, so they move to the water surface; a thin kerosene layer separates water from air and stops them from obtaining air. If larvae and pupae cannot reach air at the water surface, they cannot respire, and the mosquito life cycle is disrupted before adulthood. The learner correctly applies this rule: Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water but require air to respire, so they move to the water surface; a thin kerosene layer separates water from air and stops them from obtaining air. Anything that lives in water gets everything it needs from the water.
